reason: The three item-level claims, supplier uses, example computations, primary-source qualifications, and both body-free compact pages pass substantive review. Owner reconciliation is needed for the ML-51 page prerequisite.

findings.reason: The approved ML-62 scope calls ML-51 a prerequisite for the loss convention. Its actual supplier, def-latent-class-contrastive-learning, defines iid one-negative latent-class triplets with hinge/logistic losses; this page's def-symmetric-image-text-contrastive-loss defines an N-by-N index-matched symmetric softmax and disclaims latent-class and sampling assumptions. No interface bridges these conventions, and the local CLIP definition does not use an ML-51 result. The smallest missing prerequisite is an owner-approved clarification that ML-51 is context-only or a valid specific interface. The A page directly carries the edge; the B page inherits it through multimodal-contrastive-alignment-and-transfer.

consumer_checks.reason: Its required ML-51 loss-convention edge needs owner reconciliation; its two placed items are def-symmetric-image-text-contrastive-loss and alg-zero-shot-prompt-classification.
This page requires the A page and inherits its unresolved ML-51 prerequisite; it places ex-prompt-and-distribution-sensitive-transfer.

The definition is well-defined under its stated nonzero and finite-batch assumptions, and its exponential, logarithm, and encoder suppliers support the uses made. It does not rely on the ML-51 loss convention.

The finite inputs, nonzero conditions, prototype normalization, softmax, and least-index tie rule specify a well-defined procedure; its use of the shared embedding and positive scale suppliers is sound.

The prompt rankings, semantic-similarity contrast, and finite source/target errors check out. Its reported CLIP results and limitations match Radford et al., §§2–5 and 6 [primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.00020).
